articles.title_zh: Wall Street ends lower as Alphabet revenue miss revives AI capex jitters
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
By Stephen Culp and Shashwat Chauhan
NEW YORK, Oct 29 (Reuters) - US stocks slid on Thursday, with investors reassessing big tech's massive AI spending spree as they digested high-profile earnings and crucial inflation data the day after the Federal Reserve held US interest ‌rates steady.
All three major US equity indexes lost ground, with the tech-laden Nasdaq losing the most in the wake of Alphabet's ‌disappointing quarterly results released late Wednesday.
In contrast, the smallcap Russell 2000 advanced 1.0%.
Semiconductor stocks snapped their four-day winning streak, dropping 1.4% as investors sought to distinguish between companies that can fund ​their lofty AI ambitions and those that burn through cash and borrow funds to realize their goals.
Alphabet was in the latter camp following its quarterly report released late on Wednesday. The Google parent's revenue miss was compounded by its accelerated AI-related cash burn. Its shares slid 12.6%, dragging the communication services sector down with it.
"A risk-off day like this, with small caps outperforming, is a good sign that thus far the market's interpretation of cracks in the AI story ‌doesn't mean cracks in every corner of the ⁠market," said Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird in Louisville, Kentucky. "There's plenty of other places to go with your money outside of the AI trade that have pretty decent prospects."
On Wednesday, Federal Reserve policymakers chose to hold US ⁠rates steady, acknowledging that while price pressures remain "elevated," the central bank will decide on its next move as it "accumulates more information."
A raft of economic data released on Thursday answered that call, with a first take on third-quarter GDP that showed the US economy grew at a faster-than-expected pace in the third quarter, while price growth ​continued ​to heat up with a war-related oil supply crunch feeding into broader, systemic inflation.
The ​Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 132.54 points, or 0.25%, ‌to 52,342.56, the S&P 500 lost 23.59 points, or 0.30%, to 7,720.39 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 365.13 points, or 1.37%, to 26,184.72.
Third-quarter earnings season has crossed the halfway point, with 253 of the companies in the S&P 500 having reported. Of those, 81% have beaten analyst expectations, according to the most recent LSEG data.
Analysts now expect aggregate third-quarter S&P 500 earnings growth of 31.0%, year-on-year, per LSEG.
Caterpillar topped quarterly profit estimates but left its growth targets unchanged. The heavy equipment maker's shares tumbled 9.3%.
Eli Lilly jumped 6.6% after the drugmaker lifted its revenue outlook on strong sales of weight-loss drugs.
Ford ‌gained 12.4% following the automaker's third-quarter revenue beat.
Merck beat earnings expectations on the strength ​of its cancer drug Keytruda and its HPV vaccine Gardasil. The drugmaker's shares advanced 3.8%.
Software ​stocks were broadly weak. Fortinet and ServiceNow both dropped more than ​20% after reporting their quarterly results.
Marvell Technology slumped 13.2% after media reports said the company was in advanced talks ‌to buy data-center optics maker Lumentum Holdings. Lumentum shares rose ​0.6%.
Amazon dropped 6.5% in extended trading after ​it provided disappointing fourth-quarter sales guidance.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.95-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 146 new highs and 201 new lows on the NYSE.
On the Nasdaq, 2,464 stocks rose and 2,308 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.07-to-1 ratio.
The ​S&P 500 posted 19 new 52-week highs and 6 ‌new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 88 new highs and 191 new lows.
Volume on US exchanges was 17.05 billion shares, ​compared with the 17.09 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.
(Reporting by Stephen Culp; Additional ​reporting by Shashwat Chauhan and Utkarsh Hathi in Bengaluru; Editing by David Gregorio)

articles.title_orig: Israel election result shows no overall majority as vote count complete
articles.title_zh: Israel election result shows no overall majority as vote count complete
articles.content_orig:
Vote counting is complete in Israel’s elections with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition winning a majority in parliament, Israeli media have said.
As the provisional results were being published on Thursday, opposition politicians met to explore options for a coalition.
With more than 99 percent of Tuesday’s ballots tallied, Netanyahu’s bloc held 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset while the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot secured 48 seats, Israeli outlet Haaretz reported. The Arab list parties, meanwhile, held a combined 19 seats, it added.
Both Netanyahu’s bloc and the opposition parties fell short of securing the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority.
The final results of the Knesset elections will be certified and announced by Wednesday. Until that date, the results are subject to change.
Tuesday’s elections – the first since the October 7, 2023, attacks on southern Israel and the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza – were widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s premiership.
On Thursday, Eisenkot, who heads the Yashar party, met former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the Together party, to discuss ways to form a new government “as quickly as possible”, according to a statement reported by Israel’s Ynet News outlet.
Eisenkot also met Democrats party chairman Yair Golan, the only member of the opposition alliance to support forming a coalition with parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, while all other political groups have rejected any such union.
Golan met separately with Mansour Abbas, who leads the United Arab list, or Ra’am, which is projected to win seven of the 19 Arab party seats.
“This is a time for action. Our responsibility is not to miss the opportunity for change and the salvation of Israel,” Golan said in a post on X after his meeting with Abbas.
Al Jazeera correspondent Nour Odeh noted that “Eisenkot has an uphill battle ahead of him.”
The former military leader-turned-politician has pledged “not to ally himself or get into a partnership with the Palestinian Israeli parties”, Odeh said, reporting from the occupied West Bank because Al Jazeera is banned from Israel.
But given the fact that no political bloc has a majority, the Eisenkot-led opposition bloc cannot form a governing coalition without the support of Arab-led parties, she added.
Meanwhile, Netanyahu’s Likud party has continued to amplify unsubstantiated allegations that Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, potentially with foreign assistance – claims that have been rejected .
The head of the Central Elections Committee, Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, said “serious suspicions” of foreign interference had been brought to him in a letter to the Shin Bet security agency. Sohlberg said he could not verify the claims, but given their serious nature, he asked the agency to investigate.
Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of working to delegitimise the election results with his allegations.
In a video posted on his X account, Eisenkot said: “The days of Netanyahu using state institutions against Israeli interests for his personal needs are over,” adding that no “spin” can change voters rejecting his government at the polls.
“Benjamin Netanyahu is not satisfied with the results, no matter how much he has been saying that he won,” political analyst Xavier Abu Eid told Al Jazeera.
He added that while it seems unlikely the opposition could take advantage by overcoming differences with the Arab-led groups, there could be an understanding to replace the current speaker of the Knesset, who is close to Netanyahu.
“If there is a new speaker in the Knesset, … Netanyahu loses an important ally,” Abu Eid said, adding that this might give an opening for the opposition to “actually start passing legislation” against him.
Odeh said the next steps would involve negotiations between political groups after the Central Elections Committee announces and certifies the election results by Wednesday.

articles.title_orig: Robust consumer spending, AI-related investment power US economy in third quarter
articles.title_zh: Robust consumer spending, AI-related investment power US economy in third quarter
articles.content_orig:
The pace of price increases stepped up in September, keeping inflation well above the Federal Reserve's target, while the economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter, according to Commerce Department reports Thursday.
The personal consumption expenditures price index increased a seasonally adjusted 0.5% for the month, putting the annual inflation rate at 3.6%. The monthly increase was the largest since March but in line with the Dow Jones consensus, while the annual rate was 0.1 percentage point below.
Excluding food and energy, the core PCE posted respective readings of 0.3% and 3.1%, in line with the consensus. While the Fed follows both measures closely, officials generally see the core reading as more indicative of longer-term inflation trends.
While inflation continued to run ahead of the Fed's 2% target, the Commerce Department also reported that gross domestic product was strong in the third quarter.
GDP increased at a seasonally adjusted annualized pace of 3.4%, better than the 3.1% estimate and well ahead of the 2.2% in the second quarter.
Also, in September consumer spending proved resilient, climbing 0.5%, a bit below the forecast for a 0.6% gain, while personal income rose 0.2%, compared with the estimate for 0.3%.
The reports come the day after the Fed voted to hold its benchmark interest rate in a range between 3.75%-4%. Despite elevated inflation readings, central bank officials insist they can afford to evaluate incoming data before deciding on their next move.
"The period right in front of us is information rich. There is a lot that's happening in the world. My colleagues and I are keen to take notice of it," Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said Wednesday.
However, the data deluge from Thursday shows the Fed could have more work to do.
A Labor Department report also released Thursday showed that layoffs remain low. Initial jobless claims edged lower to a seasonally adjusted 194,000 for the week ended Oct. 24, below the estimate for 200,000 and near levels last seen in the late 1960s.
Stock market future s were negative following the releases while Treasury yields also fell.
"Net, net, economic growth is powering ahead despite the uncertainty of geopolitical risks and the damage posed to many sectors of the economy by higher energy costs," said Chris Rupkey, chief economist at Fwdbonds. "The economy was thought to have been a lost cause during much of the current Administration's time in office, but real GDP has bounced back above a 3 percent run rate in Q3 2026 for the first time in a year."
Economic growth has been driven by higher levels of investment from the artificial intelligence build-out, as well as high levels of consumer and government spending.
Consumer spending rose 3.8% in the third quarter, the same pace as the prior period. Gross private domestic investment soared 19.4%, driven by a 20.9% surge in equipment spending and an 8.4% jump on intellectual property products.
Real sales to private domestic purchasers, a proxy that Fed officials use for underlying demand, rose 4.9%, compared with a 4.6% increase in the second quarter.
There was some good inflation news for the period: On a quarterly basis, PCE prices rose 2.1% on the headline number and 2.5% for core, down respectively from 5% and 3.3% in the second quarter.
September's price increases were driven largely by a surge in energy costs that economists fear could be spreading to other parts of the economy. Gasoline and other energy goods saw a 9.2% rise for the month while energy goods and services broadly jumped 5.4%.
At the same time, services prices excluding energy and housing rose 0.4%, and housing costs increased 0.3%.

Third quarter earnings season is in full swing this week, with corporate results dropping from Big Tech heavy-hitters Microsoft ( MSFT ), Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and Amazon ( AMZN ).

Aside from Big Tech, industries from oil to chips to pharmaceuticals will be represented, as Exxon Mobil ( XOM ), Intel ( INTC ), Boeing ( BA ), Ford ( F ), and Eli Lilly ( LLY ) also open their books.
It's shaping up to be another strong earnings season. According to FactSet data , nearly a quarter of S&P 500 companies have already reported Q3 earnings so far, with an overall earnings growth rate of 29.5%. If that rate holds, it will mark the third straight quarter of earnings growth above 25%.
Sandisk ( SNDK ) stock climbed in extended trading after solid across-the-board earnings and guidance beats.
Notably, Sandisk announced it will enact an eight-for-one stock split, effective Nov. 19.
This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.

The NAND flash memory maker has been a key beneficiary of the AI data center boom.
"We have started fiscal year 2027 with another quarter of strong performance, with robust and growing demand for our products driving outpaced growth in our data center business," CEO David Goeckeler said in a press release.
The stock has soared in 2026, but it's had a rocky few months as of late. Year to date, shares are up over 460%, but the stock has largely treaded water since July.
Reddit ( RDDT ) stock plunged 17% after hours. The company reported better-than-expected third quarter earnings and revenue, but investors were disappointed by softer-than-expected US daily active users and a subdued fourth quarter outlook.
Here's what Reddit reported in the third quarter, compared to analyst estimates compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence:

Global daily active users (DAUs): increased 12% year over year to 130.3 million

Amazon ( AMZN ) reported third quarter results Thursday, missing on the top and bottom lines, sending the stock falling.
Follow live updates from the report and earnings call here >
Starbucks ( SBUX ) earnings beat expectations on Thursday, as the company looked to move beyond its turnaround plan to accelerate growth.
For the fifth consecutive quarter, the coffee giant posted better-than-expected same-store sales growth, up 7.2%, compared to Wall Street's expectations of 6.2%. That was driven by US sales, which were up 7.7%, with roughly a 5% increase in ticket sizes as customers spent more at Starbucks and roughly a 2% increase in transactions.
"We have a clear plan. We've been working the plan. And the plan is working," CEO Brian Niccol said in prepared remarks. He added that the company is "operating with greater consistency" and that more customers are going to Starbucks.
Adjusted earnings came in at $0.80, more than the $0.71 Wall Street forecast. Revenue fell short, at $9.1 billion, compared with the $9.2 billion the Street was looking for, reflecting the sale of Starbucks China business.
International sales fell short of Wall Street's expectations, rising just 0.9% compared to the roughly 3% growth the Street was looking for.
Intel ( INTC ) reported better-than-anticipated third-quarter earnings after the bell Thursday, but Q4 revenue outlook fell short of Wall Street's expectations on declining PC sales.
Intel stock fell more than 20% on the news.
In the fourth quarter, Intel is projecting revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, well below the $17 billion analysts expected.
Intel says the shortfall is a result of a worse-than-anticipated drop in PC revenue. The industry is contending with two overlapping factors at the moment: difficult comparisons to last year, when Microsoft ended support for Windows 10, forcing enterprises around the world to purchase newer Windows 11 systems, and the steady increase in PC prices, which is eating into demand.
Rivian ( RIVN ) reported upbeat third quarter results after the bell on Thursday and boosted its guidance, citing strong R2 sales.
Rivian reported Q3 revenue of $2.155 billion vs. $2.02 billion per Bloomberg consensus, up 38% from a year ago. Rivian posted an adjusted loss per share of $0.48 vs. $0.61, and an adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization) loss of $435 million vs. $575.9 million, narrower than the $602 million loss from last year.
Rivian also reported a gross profit of $176 million, up $152 million from a quarter ago, though the automotive segment remained negative.
Rivian stock gained on the news.
Crocs ( CROX ) stock soared 25% on Thursday to its highest price in over two years as investors cheered on a return to growth for the footwear company's HeyDude loafer brand and a brighter outlook for 2026 sales.
In the third quarter, HeyDude revenue increased 6.1% over the previous year to $170 million, marking the first sales increase in six quarters for the struggling shoe brand.
Crocs bought HeyDude for $2.5 billion in 2022, its largest acquisition ever. But the brand struggled amid excess inventory and discounting, causing investors to become fed up with lagging sales.
HeyDude makes up roughly 16% of Crocs' total revenue, while the flagship Crocs brand accounts for the remaining 84% of sales.
Caterpillar ( CAT ) reported and a record order backlog of $78.1 billion in the third quarter, but the stock fell 11% in premarket trading as Wall Street set a high bar and AI-related stocks broadly got hit.
The company has become a growing industrial AI play as its power generation business, which makes and services turbines, has gotten a boost amid booming data center construction.

Analysts may be down on the stock as they were hoping for raised guidance and a wider sales beat.
"Our third-quarter results reflect the durability of our end markets, with strong order rates and a record backlog," Caterpillar CEO Joe Creed said in the release. Prime Minister Mark Carney is set to host European leaders in Canada as he seeks to deepen trade ties with the EU amid Donald Trump’s ongoing economic hostility.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa will join Carney in Montreal on Thursday for a two-day summit.
It is understood the talks will aim to deepen trade, defence and economic relationships as Canada looks to secure relationships outside of Washington.
EU officials said ahead of the talks that the proposed partnership with Canada could improve the relationship more than has ever been achieved with a non-European country.
Carney said Tuesday the summit would launch further negotiations over the next year. “It doesn’t matter about specific names or nomenclature,” Carney said.
“What matters is the difference that it will make to lives of Canadians, young Canadians in terms of opportunities to study, work and travel, our Canadian businesses in terms of new opportunities, Canadian researchers in terms of depths of opportunity, and Canada as a whole becoming a more independent, more sovereign nation, so we can live our lives as we choose.”
Carney has ruled out formally joining the EU, which would require Canada to align its laws and regulations with the bloc’s.
Canadian officials said Canada would not assume the EU’s membership-related budget obligations, although it could contribute to specific programs. Carney has said any enhanced partnership would face a vote in Canada’s Parliament.
The summit puts Carney’s vision for a new global order to the test. At the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, in January, he warned that the U.S.-led international order was breaking down and urged middle powers to unite against economic coercion.
Trump has suggested Canada’s proposed EU arrangement could be a “hostile act” and threatened tariffs on Europe if he considered it unfriendly.
Asked Wednesday about possible retaliation, a senior Canadian government official told reporters the closer relationship was not directed against the United States but reflected longstanding shared interests.
The summit is expected to launch an “Alliance for the Future,” a framework for closer cooperation on trade, defense, critical minerals, technology and research. Von der Leyen said the alliance would help Canada and Europe respond together to a world of growing rivalries.
The proposed relationship could include regular meetings between Canadian ministers and European commissioners and expanded opportunities for students through the EU’s Erasmus+ program, which supports international study and educational exchanges.
European commissioners and Canadian Cabinet ministers will hold sector-specific meetings, beginning with a business forum Thursday before formal leaders’ talks Friday. Officials hope to develop the broader partnership for possible endorsement in 2027.
Tobias Gehrke, a senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, said the disagreement over terminology was unlikely to derail closer cooperation.
“There is no magic shortcut to rapidly reducing Europe’s and Canada’s reliance on the U.S. economy and military — not least since Washington might retaliate,” Gehrke said. “But the political window is now wide open to take a much bigger step than was previously conceivable.”
Canada has long looked to Europe to reduce its dependence on its much larger southern neighbor. “It was the idea of not being alone with the Americans that drove it,” said Robert Bothwell, a University of Toronto historian.
Carney has deep personal ties to Europe. The former Bank of Canada governor led the Bank of England from 2013 to 2020.
He chose Paris and London for his first foreign trip as prime minister rather than Washington, a break with tradition. He said the countries reflected Canada’s founding Indigenous, French and British peoples.
Daniel Béland, a political science professor at McGill University in Montreal, said Trump’s policies are accelerating Canada’s efforts to strengthen ties beyond the United States.
“The policies and rhetoric of the Trump administration are clearly pushing both Canada and the EU to imagine a world without strong U.S. leadership and to act accordingly,” Béland said.
Ottawa is reviewing plans to buy 72 additional American-made F-35 fighter jets and considering Sweden’s Saab Gripen as an alternative. Canada has committed to an initial 16 F-35s.
Canada is the only non-European country participating in the EU’s 150-billion-euro ($167-billion) SAFE defense procurement program, allowing Canadian companies to take part in joint European military purchases.
But deeper defense cooperation faces obstacles. Sundar said France is pushing for strict “Made in Europe” rules that could limit Canadian companies’ access to future EU defense spending, while Germany favors broader participation by countries outside the bloc.
He said negotiations over the EU’s next seven-year budget could matter more to Canada than anything announced in Montreal.
The two sides already have a sweeping free trade agreement, known as CETA, that eliminated most tariffs. Most provisions have been in force since 2017, although some EU member states have yet to ratify it.
The United States accounted for 71.7% of Canada’s merchandise exports in 2025. Carney wants to double exports to other countries over the next decade.
Canada and the EU are pursuing closer cooperation on digital trade and critical minerals, including possible European Investment Bank financing. Canadian officials said Wednesday they were exploring ways to stabilize mineral prices and encourage investment.
Gehrke said Europe’s growing trade confrontation with China is driving demand for Canadian critical minerals. Canada has the resources and mining expertise Europe needs, while Europe offers industrial demand, technology and capital.
Sundar said the shifting international order presents Europe with an opportunity to become a more influential global power.
“Trump’s predatory behavior is allowing the EU to position itself as an alternative geopolitical anchor,” he said.

Microsoft is now rolling out a revamped right-click menu in Windows 11. This new feature is included in the optional KB5127936 preview update , released on October 28th for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2.
One of the biggest changes in this update is the ability to customize the right-click menu to your own preferences. Using the new “Customize menu” option at the bottom of the right-click menu, you can choose which commands and app features should be displayed.
For example, you can add or remove the “Print” command, hide options you don’t use, and choose which add-ons from installed apps should appear, whether directly in the menu or placed in a sub-menu.
Microsoft also makes it possible to display “Cut,” “Copy,” “Paste,” “Rename,” “Delete,” and “Share” as standard menu options instead of the row of special icons that was introduced with Windows 11. This allows you to restore some of the look and feel of Windows 10.
According to Microsoft, the right-click menu has also been optimized to open more quickly and appear less cluttered.
To install the update, navigate to Settings → Windows Update → Advanced options → Optional updates, locate the KB5127936 update, and click the button to download and install.
These right-click menu changes are still being rolled out gradually, which means not all users will have access to the new “Customize menu” feature straight away, even after installing the update.
This article originally appeared on our sister publication PC för Alla and was translated and localized from Swedish.
Andreas has worked as a technology journalist for many years. Andreas's interest in technology started with the Nokia 6110 about a thousand years ago, and today he follows AI development with both delight and horror.

Reddit has long attracted millions of users to its site through Google, with many even appending the word “Reddit” to their search queries for better answers. But as search traffic dries up amid the shift to AI-powered search, Reddit is rethinking its relationship with the open internet. In its third-quarter earnings call on Thursday, the company announced it’s transitioning to a primarily “logged-in experience.”
The move is designed to protect its data from AI scraping, allowing the company to instead forge lucrative licensing deals with model providers. But just as important, such a shift could help Reddit to increase its revenue even as it faces daily active user declines in its largest market, the U.S.
Overall, Reddit’s global daily active users were flat quarter-over-quarter in Q3, reaching 130.3 million, while U.S. daily active users dropped from 53.2 million in Q2 to 50.7 million in Q3 and were down 2% year-over-year.
The company is not alone in seeing such declines; the shift to an AI-centered web has impacted most websites and publishers by now, leading to fewer click-throughs, as AI summaries provide answers that don’t require website visits and Google’s traditional “ten blue links” have reduced relevance. (The change is now even impacting Google’s bottom line , its earnings revealed.)
But at Reddit’s scale, the numbers associated with such a decline are enormous. The company said search traffic referrals dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week in October. It warned that if the trend continues, daily active users could decline to a low-double-digit percentage by next quarter. (To play that out: a hypothetical 10% to 12% decline could bring Reddit to roughly 115 million to 117 million daily actives, down from 130.3 million in Q3. That’s a huge drop!)
At the same time, Reddit has gotten significantly better at monetizing its audience even as its growth weakens. Revenue increased 53% year-over-year to $895 million, ahead of Wall Street’s expectations of about $875 million. Net income rose 74% to $283 million. Advertising revenue grew 54% to $847 million while nonadvertising revenue, which includes its AI data-licensing business, grew 35% year-over-year to $48 million.
And despite a 2% year-over-year decline in U.S. daily users, Reddit’s average revenue per daily active user in the U.S. rose 53% to $13.82. Globally, average revenue per daily active user increased 36% year-over-year to $6.87.
Shifting to a logged-in experience could boost those numbers even higher because logged-in users are typically worth more to advertisers.
Unlike the logged-out users who often find their way to the site via search, logged-in users provide more signals about their interests and behaviors, which helps to better target and personalize ads.
Those same signals would also help Reddit provide a more personalized experience to its users, which includes personalized feeds, recommendations of new communities to subscribe to, and pushes to vote, comment, participate, and more. (This also includes pushing recommendations to its new algorithmic “For You” feed, announced yesterday , which will combine posts from communities users belong to alongside other recommendations based on their interests.)
Still, a change of this magnitude could be the canary in the coal mine for the open web.
“I don’t know about you, but as someone whose life has been defined by the open internet, it’s a big change for me,” wrote Reddit co-founder and CEO Steve Huffman in a post published on Reddit’s site . “But I’ve come to the conclusion that this is the right decision for our platform and the right decision for our business,” he said.
The company notes that the shift to the logged-in experience will not be an overnight change; it will first run tests in select markets outside the U.S. in the fourth quarter. It doesn’t yet have a timeline for when the change will be rolled out to all its users worldwide. It also acknowledged that access to a logged-out front page is important.
Plus, Reddit pointed out that being logged in doesn’t mean having to give up anonymity, nor will it remove its option to browse anonymously through its “incognito mode” experience, which is being rebuilt.
“There are still plenty of questions that are unanswered, particularly around where the boundaries should be between logged-in and logged-out experiences,” Hoffman wrote. “This is a big evolution for Reddit, and not one we’re taking lightly. But I believe it’s the right next step for the platform and for our future.”

articles.title_zh: Reddit shares sink on weak sales guidance and plans login requirement test as Google search traffic shrinks
articles.content_orig:
Reddit plans to require all users to create official accounts to access the social media platform, marking a major departure for the site known as "the front page of the internet."
The company revealed the change Thursday as part of its third-quarter earnings, in which it beat on the top and bottom lines, but provided weak fourth-quarter sales guidance. The company's shares dropped over 15% after its numbers were released.
Here's how the company did compared with LSEG estimates:
Reddit CEO Steve Huffman told CNBC in an interview that the company's shrinking search-referral traffic from Google played a major role in its planned efforts to require people to become "logged-in" users.
A previous Google search update designed to surface "authentic" content from internet forums helped Reddit grow its user base over the past few years, but the search giant's continued push on AI overviews and related chatting features has negatively impacted referral traffic .
"I think fundamentally that relationship between Google and the rest of the internet is evolving, and so for us, this means a continued focus on our core users that come to Reddit directly," Huffman said.
Previous Google algorithm changes would "kind of come and go," Huffman said, but the company's AI efforts represent "a fundamental shift in how the Google product works, from being a traffic driver to whatever's going on now."
Huffman didn't provide any specific timing on when Reddit plans for the platform registration change, saying only that implementing it through the site would involve a lot of complexity . The company will begin testing in the fourth quarter outside of the U.S.
He said that Reddit is still determining what parts of the service logged-out users will be able to see, and will iron out the details as part of its upcoming testing.
Reddit said that daily active uniques, or DAUq, rose 12% year-over-year to 130.3 million in the third quarter, trailing Wall Street estimates of 133.7 million. U.S.-specific DAUq dropped 2% year-over-year to 50.7 million, which was below analyst projections of 53.5 million.
Huffman said that "search referral traffic is down meaningfully in this quarter" and that the trend will continue in the fourth quarter.
He said that Reddit is continuing its effort to make its platform "a daily habit" for users. "So that's where our focus is: growing those app users and logged-in users," Huffman said.
Reddit, which derives the bulk of its overall sales from online advertising, is able to monetize logged-ln users better than logged-out users , because those registered users are more active and valuable to advertisers itching to deliver more targeted ads.
"The vast majority of our revenue comes from our app users and logged-in users are direct traffic, and both of those are up Q. over Q. and so that's where our focus is," Huffman said.
The company's third-quarter sales grew 53% year-over-year, marking an end to the eight-straight quarters of revenue growth eclipsing 60% that it reported in July as part of its second-quarter earnings.
Reddit said that fourth-quarter sales will come in a range of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, which was below Wall Street estimates of $1.05 billion.
"It's still a strong guide," Huffman said about its revenue guidance. "We are still growing at an industry leading rate, and that's despite the headwinds from search referrals."
Reddit's third-quarter average revenue per user, or ARPU, came in at $6.87, which was higher than the $6.50 that analysts were expecting.
The company's "other revenue" segment, which includes its data-licensing business, jumped 35% year-over-year to $48 million in the third quarter. Reddit's two biggest data-licensing partners are OpenAI and Google.
Huffman said that Reddit remains "in negotiations" with Google over its data-licensing agreement, and said that it is "only going to do a deal that makes sense for Reddit," if it chooses to continue the partnership.
"I think there's a lot of strategic considerations that goes into that," Huffman said.
Huffman called the required registration plan a "big change" for himself, considering he "grew up on the open Internet."
"Reddit is the last platform to provide basically unfettered logged-out access, and that's largely because of me, I've been holding that line," Huffman, a Reddit co-founder, said. "I think users will probably go through the same understanding that I have, which is that it's a sign of the times. It's an evolution of how these platforms work."
Huffman later expanded on the significance of AI's impact on Reddit's user growth in an earnings call with analysts, and explained that the company plans to continue spending on marketing efforts intended to offset search-referral declines. "This is a consequential time for Reddit, and this period does remind me of about 11 years ago when I came back to the company," Huffman told analysts, referring to when he rejoined Reddit in 2015 following it's then-chief Ellen Pao stepping down. "We had a lot of conversations then about what is Reddit and what is Reddit for, and what is our place in this ecosystem. And we've been having those conversations at Reddit recently." "Reddit's mission is to create community and belonging for everyone in the world, and while there's overlap between Reddit and other players in the ecosystem, whether we're talking about social media or AI search, fundamentally, Reddit is communities and conversations," Huffman said.

articles.title_orig: Reddit will force everyone to log in
articles.title_zh: Reddit will force everyone to log in
articles.content_orig:
Reddit is becoming a ‘logged-in-only experience,’ says CEO Steve Huffman.
Reddit is becoming a ‘logged-in-only experience,’ says CEO Steve Huffman.
Reddit is announcing a huge shift: It’s going to start requiring users to log in.
Right now, you can browse Reddit without having an account, and the site is generally a great resource for crowdsourced information on a whole range of topics. I know I’m not the only person who appends “reddit” to a lot of Google searches to find answers to things written by actual humans instead of robots . But that openness has made it a target for scraping and automated traffic, leading Reddit to file lawsuits over alleged unauthorized access of its data and make product changes like limiting access to “Old Reddit.”
There’s no definitive timeline on when this change will roll out to all users, or how the site will work if you’re logged out. (If I send my friend a link to a thread and they aren’t logged in, what will they see?) To start, Reddit will test the logged-in requirement in “select markets outside the US” in the “coming months,” according to CEO Steve Huffman . “We’ll look at the impact on the user experience, on our business, and on the whole Reddit ecosystem, figure out where the right boundaries are, and go from there.” Reddit has also rebuilt and is rereleasing the Reddit app’s incognito mode.
Huffman claims the login requirement is better for Reddit’s user experience and its ads business and is “more protective of Reddit data.” The “vast majority” of unauthorized Reddit access happens “through our logged-out experiences,” though the company will still strike licensing deals of its data with companies, like the deals it made with OpenAI and Google in 2024. Huffman notes that Reddit does not need to know a logged-in user’s identity — “Honestly, we don’t want to know” — just that the user is logged in at all. And he says that more logged-in users lets the company deliver “more relevant ads.”
“This is a big change for Reddit, where we’ve allowed logged-out access to basically all of Reddit for the last two decades,” Huffman says. “And I don’t know about you, but as someone whose life has been defined by the open internet, it’s a big change for me. But I’ve come to the conclusion that this is the right decision for our platform and the right decision for our business.”
Reddit is making this announcement alongside its Q3 2026 earnings, which were released today . Search traffic was “down meaningfully” in Q3, Huffman says in the company’s shareholder letter , with logged-out traffic and web traffic being the most heavily impacted. “During October, we have seen that search traffic has dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week,” Huffman says.
However, Huffman notes that app and logged-in daily active unique users make up “over 80% of the monetization on Reddit,” which he says “speaks to the strength of Reddit as a destination and the impact of our ongoing product work.”

articles.title_orig: A Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Nvidia’s CEO, Jensen Huang, was found to be passing intelligence to Beijing.
articles.title_zh: A Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Nvidia’s CEO, Jensen Huang, was found to be passing intelligence to Beijing.
articles.content_orig:
By WILL POTTER, US SENIOR NEWS REPORTER
Published: 09:27 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 13:07 EDT, 29 October 2026
Nvidia boss Jensen Huang sparked intelligence fears after he formed a 'close relationship' with a female spy who the CIA believed was smuggling AI microchips to China , reports say.
The AI chief, 63, reportedly alarmed the White House and US intelligence circles when it was revealed that he had formed a relationship with Chinese business executive and suspected spy Alice Huang.
As the CEO of tech firm Megaspeed, Ms Huang, of no relation to the Nvidia boss, is believed to have acted as an intermediary funneling banned AI chips to China, according to The New York Times .
The efforts allegedly violated US policies preventing Nvidia's advanced AI chips from reaching Beijing , with the company playing a central role in America's race to control the artificial intelligence industry.
Sources told the Times that the relationship only became known when an investigation was launched into Ms Huang's alleged espionage for China, and intelligence circles discovered a US citizen was 'in contact' with her.
When top officials requested to learn the name of the US citizen, they were stunned to learn that it was Jensen Huang, one of the richest and most powerful men in the world.
It is unclear when the relationship began or when it was uncovered, however, President Trump was reportedly briefed on the intelligence findings roughly one year ago, the Times reported.
Trump, who has often spoken of the vital need to win the AI race over China, chose not to act on the information related to Huang.
Nvidia boss Jensen Huang sparked intelligence fears after he formed a 'close relationship' with female spy Alice Huang (center) who the CIA believed was smuggling AI microchips to China, reports say
Huang reportedly set off alarm bells in the White House and US intelligence circles with his 'close relationship' with the suspected Chinese spy
Huang's Nvidia has grown to a market capitalization of over $5 trillion, and the company represents the central pillar in America's AI expansionist efforts.
With Trump embracing Silicon Valley and technology executives in his second term, Huang has found his way into the president's inner circle at times, often invited to the White House with other business titans.
Huang has successfully lobbied the Trump administration to loosen regulations on AI technology and restrictions on the sales of Nvidia chips around the world. In June, Huang revealed to The Associated Press that Trump often called him late at night to discuss AI, jobs, manufacturing and national security.
It was also revealed earlier this month that Trump bought as much as $1.6 million in Nvidia stock and sold over $1 million of the stock in August, and Trump has often placed Huang next to himself at state dinners in his second term.
But according to The New York Times, Huang's proximity to the president escalated at the same time that his 'close relationship' with Ms Huang was attracting the attention of US intelligence.
A probe into the Megaspeed CEO's ties to Beijing determined that she was gathering intelligence for China and diverting Nvidia chips into the country.
Huang has become a key business titan in Trump's second term, and the president often places himself next to the Nvidia chief at White House summits
Huang seen with his wife Lori in April 2026
Pictures posted to LinkedIn by the company NetThunder showed the Nvidia boss and Ms Huang together in a bar in Taipei in June 2024
Yet while she remains under surveillance, companies that have been affiliated with her have continued to purchase Nvidia chips this year, per the Times.
Sources told the Times that while some top American business leaders receive defense briefings if they are targeted by foreign intelligence services, Mr Huang has not received these briefings from the US.
When Trump was briefed over the claims last year, officials said they did not believe the Nvidia boss knew that Ms Huang was gathering information for Beijing.
Although it is unclear when the relationship is believed to have begun, in June 2024 the pair were seen together at a bar in Taipei following a local technology trade show.
Huang, in a black leather jacket, was seen sipping whiskey with other executives in the dark bar, as Ms Huang sat next to him. The pictures were shared to LinkedIn at the time by the company NetThunder.
A year later in May 2025, the pair were again seen leaving a restaurant together in Taipei, following a business dinner with AI suppliers. According to the Times, she waited behind for Huang as he spoke to journalists.
Nvidia said in response to the allegations that Megaspeed was like many of its regional partners, and that an internal investigation previously debunked claims it was smuggling chips into China.
Huang has made a number of appearances with Trump in his second term, and the Nvidia boss revealed earlier this year that the president often calls him late at night
Huang's Nvidia has grown to a market capitalization of over $5 trillion, and the company represents the central pillar in America's AI expansionist efforts
A spokesman for Nvidia said: 'Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year.'
The spokesman added that Nvidia is 'confident that if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.'
Megaspeed also said in a statement that its 'current leadership' was taking the matter 'extremely seriously and is committed to getting to the facts behind these allegations.'
The company added that 'outside counsel has been retained to conduct a thorough internal investigation and has notified the U.S. government that we are fully committed to cooperating.'
The Daily Mail has contacted Nvidia and the White House for comment.

articles.title_orig: Rivian third-quarter earnings beat estimates as software revenue, R2 deliveries rise
articles.title_zh: Rivian third-quarter earnings beat estimates as software revenue, R2 deliveries rise
articles.content_orig:
Rivian Automotive beat Wall Street's third-quarter earnings expectations as it ramped up production of its new R2 entry-level SUV that the company has promised investors will lead it to profitability.
Here's how Rivian performed in the period ended Sept. 30, compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG:
Shares of Rivian were up roughly 7% during afterhours trading Thursday, after hitting a new 52-week low of $11.38 earlier in the day. The stock closed at $11.45 a share, down 1.9%
The electric vehicle maker also revised its 2026 guidance to mark expected improvements in its vehicle deliveries, pre-tax adjusted earnings and capital expenditures.
The new guidance calls for a pre-tax adjusted loss of between $1.75 billion and $1.85 billion — a $100 million improvement at the midpoint from its prior guidance — vehicle deliveries of between 67,000 and 70,000 units, up from at least 65,000; and capital expenditures of between $1.4 billion and $1.5 billion, $300 million less at the midpoint.
Rivian attributed the improvement in its pre-tax adjusted earnings guidance to better-than-expected revenue related to its sales of regulatory credits, an IEEPA tariff refund receivable in the third quarter and its expected increase in vehicle deliveries.
The R2 — the first deliveries of which arrived to customers in June — has become Rivian's best-selling model and was responsible for "much of the gain quarter-over-quarter," the company said.
Rivian delivered a record 19,248 units from July through September. The company does not disclose deliveries by vehicle.
The EV maker remains unprofitable overall but continued to narrow its losses during the quarter. The company reported a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $913 million, compared with a loss of $1.17 billion during the third quarter of 2025.
Rivian's gross profit, which is closely monitored by investors, was $176 million during the third quarter, up from $24 million a year earlier. Its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization was a loss of $435 million, a $167 million improvement from the same period last year.
The company reported that its software and services segment continues to grow, generating $605 million in revenue and a gross profit of $256 million, a 42% margin. That compares to its automotive operations, which recorded nearly $1.55 billion in revenue and a gross loss of $80 million.
Also on Thursday, Rivian reiterated that it expects the R2, a smaller and less expensive sibling to its current luxury R1S SUV, to have a positive gross margin by the end of the year. CEO RJ Scaringe has said the company needs to scale beyond current R2 production plans of 160,000 units in order to achieve overall profitability.
"That ramp-up is critical for us getting to positive gross margin on R2 and that ultimately will contribute to positive gross margin for the business," Scaringe told CNBC's Phil LeBeau during an interview Thursday. "We're going to see that through the end of the quarter and the unit economics will continue to grow … into Q1 of next year as well."
Rivian on Thursday said its cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments balance was $5.5 billion, up from $5.3 billion to end the second quarter.

articles.title_orig: What killed 500-plus penguins? How scientists solved the mystery
articles.title_zh: What killed 500-plus penguins? How scientists solved the mystery
articles.content_orig:
A small group of Adélie penguins return to their colony. A mega-colony of these penguins was hit by a big die-off in early 2024. Ralph Vanstreels hide caption
Sailing toward the Danger Islands, Dr. Ralph Vanstreels had a good idea of what he might find: A lot of dead Adélie penguins.
It was March 2024 and a virus had been sweeping through the area, leaving deceased birds in its wake.
Vanstreels got the crime right but the culprit wrong. There were dead penguins but a virus was not to blame.
As his vessel pulled up to a landing ramp on one of the islands — located just off the Antarctic Peninsula — Vanstreels and his fellow researchers immediately noticed bumps in the snow.
"Was each bump a rock or was it a carcass? We had to do quite a bit of intensive searching [through the snow]," says Vanstreels, who is based in Argentina and is a wildlife veterinarian with the University of California, Davis.
The team ultimately found more than 537 penguin carcasses on just the ramp, which he estimates was about the size of an airport runway.
There were many more carcasses elsewhere on the Danger Islands, which are home to two mega colonies for penguins. The researchers estimate there were thousands of dead Adélie penguins and other species of birds. But they had to work quickly and couldn't do a complete count, Vanstreels says.
A view of the Adélie penguin colony at Beagle Island, one of the Danger Islands. A few penguin carcasses are scattered on the rocks. Ralph Vanstreels hide caption
"You cannot stay there very long because you might be locked down with an iceberg blocking your way out," he says.
As the team has pieced together this tragic penguin mystery, Vanstreels says, the case holds broader lessons for tracking the spread of diseases globally.
Now let's time jump to Australia a few months ago for another bird disease conundrum.
In June, H5N1 — high pathogenicity avian influenza also known as bird flu — arrived in mainland Australia. Up until that point, Australia had been the only continent to dodge the virus which has traversed the globe, leaving a trail of carcasses in its path.
Since late 2021, the virus has led to the death of nearly 300 million poultry birds. Either the virus killed them or they were culled as a preventive measure to stop the spread of the disease, according to the World Animal Health Information System. Further, bird flu is estimated to have killed millions of wild animals and marine mammals, although it's hard to get an exact figure.
Researchers were amazed that Australia could stay bird-flu-free for six years. And the virus didn't take the path that scientists expected.
"We have a lot of migration of birds between Australia and Southeast Asia, so for the first few years, we're like: That's where the virus is coming from," says Dr. Amandine Gamble , an assistant professor at Cornell University in the Department of Public and Ecosystem Health.
The way bird flu eventually got there was from the other direction. It came from Antarctica likely via migrating birds.
"This is a virus that's not assisted by airplanes," Michelle Wille , senior research fellow at the Center for Pathogen Genomics at the University of Melbourne, told NPR in 2025. "This is a virus that's traveling by mass mortality after mass mortality after mass mortality after mass mortality."
So when Vanstreels set sail to check on the penguins, he assumed bird flu would be the culprit.
Bird flu arrived in Antarctica in late 2023 and early 2024. Vanstreels and his colleagues rapidly arranged for a trip to try to figure out exactly what was happening.
"The expedition was initially fully set up to look for bird flu because that was the panic," he explains, adding that ongoing fear of a continuing global panzootic — or pandemic among animals — is justified.
In several layers of warm clothes covered by protective gear — double gloves, coveralls, glasses and masks — Vanstreels and the team started taking samples of the penguin corpses they found.
"We looked a little bit stiff when walking — like a penguin walking almost — because of all the gear," he says. "We had very strict biosafety standards."
They brought samples from the deceased penguins back to a mini-lab on their boat. By evening, they had early results. But not the results they expected.
"There is bird flu here, but the virus loads are low," he recalls. "That was a little bit puzzling."
A scientist conducts the necropsy of an Adélie penguin chick collected at Heroina Island, one of the Danger Islands where disease struck. Ralph Vanstreels hide caption
The carcasses were not very old, so Vanstreels would have expected to find far more bird flu virus if that had killed the birds. Perhaps something else was the main driver? "We were unsure what was happening," he recalls.
So what killed the 500-plus penguins on the landing ramp and the many others on the island?
Back on land several months after the voyage, in the Netherlands, Vanstreels' colleagues did more investigation. "Under the microscope, you can see that there's bacteria in the tissues," he says — not virus.
They discovered a different disease, a bacterial disease that causes avian cholera (which is distinct from human cholera).
Vanstreels and his team's findings were published in October in the journal the Proceedings of the Royal Society B .
So how worried are they about avian cholera?
The disease is not considered a major threat to humans since the strain that is specialized to birds is distinct from the strain specialized to mammals. "The risk for human infection is not really that high when you see an outbreak on birds," Vanstreels says. But, it does kill birds worldwide — especially in cold environments where the bacteria thrives.
While there's not enough research to know exactly how common avian cholera is, the disease has been on the radar of scientists for decades. However, it's not exactly top of mind. The last time researchers looked for it in the Antarctic Peninsula was 25 years ago.
"One could be misled to think that: Well, that was a unique thing that happened back in 2001, and nothing's happened ever since," says Vanstreels. Instead, it is possible that avian cholera die-offs could be occurring regularly, only scientists haven't been checking.
One of his big takeaways from this bird-flu-that-turned-out-to-be-avian-cholera event?
"Yes, there is a big thing with bird flu. But we still want to keep checking for the other diseases because they might be mixing up in the middle," Vanstreels says.
Like any good mystery, the case of the cholera-stricken penguins has got scientists wondering: Whodunit?
There's a theory that avian cholera might have been introduced to Antarctica decades ago from researchers who brought poultry from the U.S., Vanstreels says.
The Adelie penguin mega-colony at Heroina Island at the peak of the breeding season. The photo was taken in January 2025, a year after the outbreak. hide caption
Gamble, of Cornell University, adds that the strain of avian cholera found in penguins in Antarctica is "very close" to the strain found 5,000 miles away on Île Amsterdam in the Southern Indian Ocean.
"Antarctica is way more connected to the rest of the world than we think it is," she says.
It's hard to track diseases in Antarctica but, she says, it's turning out to be an important piece in the global pathogen puzzle.
The work of keeping tabs on what's happening has fallen to a number of different countries since Antarctica is not governed by any one government. It was designated as a continent of peace and science by the mid 20th-century Antarctic Treaty , which now has 58 parties — among them are the U.S., France, Japan and Russia. Many nations have research stations and team up on scientific undertakings, including tracking pathogens — be it bird flu or avian cholera — that travel great distances and don't respect borders.
"So this Avian cholera outbreak is just showing this is not a unique event," says Gamble. "We really need international

articles.title_orig: Nvidia's Jensen Huang seen as target in China spy plot, report says
articles.title_zh: Nvidia's Jensen Huang seen as target in China spy plot, report says
articles.content_orig:
An Nvidia spokesperson on Thursday pushed back on a New York Times report that detailed American intelligence agencies surveilling a person close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang because they thought she could be a Chinese intelligence asset.
According to the Times report , which cited people briefed on intelligence surveillance, Alice Huang, who is linked to the Singapore-based cloud Megaspeed, developed a close relationship with Nvidia's Jensen Huang.
Intelligence agencies worried that she was a spy, helping the Chinese government gain information from Nvidia and Jensen Huang, and fretted that Nvidia's CEO had access to President Donald Trump.
The Nvidia spokesperson pushed back on the story in a statement to CNBC, saying that Singapore-based Megaspeed is another one of the company's regional cloud customers, and that Jensen Huang's interactions with its officials are not unusual, because he speaks with thousands of customers every year.
The spokesperson added that customers don't get access to Nvidia trade secrets or relevant national security information.
The report also alleged that Megaspeed was previously suspected of helping companies evade U.S. export controls on Nvidia's AI chips, which aren't allowed to be shipped to China.
Nvidia said that Megaspeed had already been investigated for evading export controls.
"The diversion allegations against this regional cloud were thoroughly investigated and debunked last year," the spokesperson said in a statement.
Nvidia implied that the U.S. government had not briefed Nvidia on Alice Huang.
"We're confident that if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know," the spokesperson said.
Nvidia has had to walk a tightrope in Washington as its AI chips have become a powerful tool for all AI developers and a bargaining chip in economic competition with China.
Politicians and analysts say that Nvidia's AI chips could be used to create Chinese military AI models, or commercial AI models that could compete and eventually surpass American technology.
As AI has become more important to the government, Nvidia's Huang has befriended Trump and has given pro-American speeches about building U.S. AI infrastructure.
Huang has appeared with Trump at state dinners, AI summits, and international trips, all while pushing for certain Nvidia chips to get a green light to be shipped to China.
Earlier this year the U.S. government cleared Nvidia's H200 chip to be shipped to China, but Chinese regulators prevented their imports. H200s are Nvidia's Hopper generation chip, not the current faster Blackwell generation currently used by American AI developers.
The Nvidia spokesperson said the Chinese government is not looking for Nvidia products from regional clouds like Megaspeed.
"Instead, the PRC government blocked U.S. AI chips, protecting its own industry and resulting in the largest write-offs in U.S. tech history," the Nvidia spokesperson said. Last year, Nvidia wrote off about $4.5 billion in Chinese-tuned AI chips.

articles.title_zh: Rivian reports upbeat Q3 results, boosts full-year guidance as R2 sales ramp up
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Rivian ( RIVN ) reported upbeat third quarter results after the bell on Thursday and boosted its guidance, citing strong R2 sales.
Rivian reported Q3 revenue of $2.155 billion vs. $2.02 billion per Bloomberg consensus, up 38% from a year ago. Rivian posted an adjusted loss per share of $0.48 vs. $0.61, and an adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization) loss of $435 million vs. $575.9 million, narrower than the $602 million loss from last year.
Rivian also reported a gross profit of $176 million, up $152 million from a quarter ago, though the automotive segment remained negative.
Rivian stock gained on the news.
This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.
More importantly, Rivian improved its full-year profit guidance, now seeing an adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.75 billion to $1.85 billion (prior $1.8 billion to $2 billion) and trimmed capital expenditures to $1.40 billion to $1.50 billion (prior $1.7 billion to $1.8 billion), topping analyst expectations of an EBITDA loss of $1.88 billion and capital expenditures of $1.75 billion, respectively.
Rivian also raised its full-year delivery guidance to 67,000 - 70,000 (prior 65,000 to 70,000 vehicles), topping analysts' consensus estimates of 67,227.
"We had great results with R2 becoming our bestselling vehicle by volume in the third quarter. Customer and media feedback on R2 has been exceptional," CEO RJ Scaringe said in a statement. "Regarding our technology roadmap, our autonomy platform is progressing rapidly, and we are super excited about Point to Point [self-driving]."
Earlier this month, Rivian said it produced 19,751 vehicles at its plant in Normal, Illinois, and delivered 19,248 during the quarter, topping Bloomberg estimates of 18,952 and 18,902, respectively. Deliveries jumped 46% from a year ago and 58% from Q2, with R2 deliveries, which began in June, most likely fueling the growth.
Rivian's cash position is also in the spotlight. Rivian ended the quarter with $5.502 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments, with $6.095 billion of total liquidity including a revolving credit facility.

articles.title_orig: Polymarket Halted International Trading After Hackers Drained Accounts
articles.title_zh: Polymarket Halted International Trading After Hackers Drained Accounts
articles.content_orig:
Some users of prediction market platform Polymarket's international exchange had funds stolen from their accounts due to a hack of an unnamed third-party provider.
Polymarket has contacted law enforcement and pledged to reimburse any affected trader. It's unclear how many users were impacted. The company's U.S. platform was not compromised.
Traders first reported on social media platforms that they were seeing unauthorized withdrawals from their accounts on Thursday afternoon. In response, the company halted trading on its international platform.
Polymarket said that it has fixed the issue on its end, and that trading resumed at 3 p.m. ET. It told users later in a chatroom on Discord that users who had less than $10,000 taken from their wallets will have funds restored by Oct. 30, and those with funds greater than that figure withdrawn will have to sign a release form to receive their restoration.
A person familiar with the matter told CNBC that the issue stemmed from a hack of DebugBear, a website performance monitoring platform. DebugBear in a post on X said that it was impacted by a security incident on Thursday. The person familiar with the Polymarket outage said that the company referred the matter to U.K. law enforcement, as that is where DebugBear is based.
DebugBear didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
An analysis of publicly-available data by two analytics firms — Betting Intelligence and Polysights — provided to CNBC said that an account on Polymarket Thursday withdrew at least $2.7 million across 710 other wallets.
"This is certainly a significant and new form of breach that we've seen on Polymarket," said Dan Zimmermann, the chief intelligence officer at Betting Intelligence. "The timing right before the midterms ...is certainly a wake up call for folks."
Polymarket's international prediction market exchange operates as a decentralized finance platform on the Polygon blockchain and is not regulated in the U.S.
The disruption comes just days before both the company's international and U.S. exchanges are expected to see heightened volumes during the U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3.
Back in June, a similar incident happened, when Polymarket said a third party vendor had been "compromised" and that the company would refund affected users.

articles.title_orig: FTC orders Delta, Uber and others to hand over data on algorithmic pricing
articles.title_zh: FTC orders Delta, Uber and others to hand over data on algorithmic pricing
articles.content_orig:
Regulator demands companies explain how and why they charge different prices for the same product or service
The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) is demanding some of the US’s biggest airlines, ride-share companies and retailers divulge how they are using algorithms and loyalty programs to target customers and drivers with different prices and wages.
Nine companies – Delta, United, JetBlue, Lyft, Uber, DoorDash, Instacart, Target and Walmart – were named in the inquiry, which comes after investigations and lawsuits alleging consumers are charged different prices based on their buying histories and drivers paid different fares based on their personal histories.
The FTC will “scrutinize the opaque methodology that some companies in these industries may be using to determine how much consumers pay or how much gig workers are paid for the same product or service”, chair Andrew Ferguson said in a statement.
US family budgets already burdened by inflation are being gouged by opaque and sometimes deceptive store pricing practices, including surveillance pricing and overcharges by Dollar General and convenience stores .
The FTC is tasked with policing “unfair or deceptive acts or practices” in industries except banking and airlines, which means it can not impose any fines or regulations on the airlines named. While the Trump administration has rolled back corporate regulations, the FTC’s consumer protection division has joined with states in some instances to pursue legal action and penalties against some companies.
Companies must “turn over information that will allow the agency to assess whether the pricing for a ticket, ride share, food delivery or other product or service varies from one person to the next based on factors such as participation in loyalty programs or analysis of personal data by super-intelligence algorithms”, the FTC said.
Several states have begun introducing legislation to ban surveillance pricing and electronic shelf labels that could be used to set different prices based on shoppers habits and online information.
The investigation follows a July 2024 inquiry by the Biden administration into surveillance pricing, which demanded information from McKinsey, JPMorgan Chase and others that offered surveillance pricing products to consumer-facing companies.
“Details like a person’s precise location or browser history can be frequently used to target individual consumers with different prices for the same goods and services,” the FTC found in January 2025.
Whether the inquiry will result in substantial changes in consumer laws or company practices is unclear.
“What we have seen so far is that they have not been using these studies that produce meaningful reports that ultimately lead to any rule-making changes,” said Rohit Chopra, a former FTC commissioner who is now head of California’s new Business and Consumer Protection Agency.

articles.title_orig: Starbucks sales miss expectations, but its U.S. turnaround is gaining steam
articles.title_zh: Starbucks sales miss expectations, but its U.S. turnaround is gaining steam
articles.content_orig:
Starbucks on Thursday reported mixed quarterly results as its international cafes underperformed expectations.
However, its U.S. turnaround continues to take hold, as its home market topped expectations during the coffee giant's final quarter of fiscal 2026.
"We enter fiscal 2027 with momentum, a clear set of priorities and higher ambitions for what Starbucks can become," CEO Brian Niccol said in a video shared on the company's website.
Starbucks is ahead of schedule to meet the fiscal 2028 targets laid out at its investor day in January, he said on the company's earnings conference call.
For fiscal 2027, Starbucks is projecting adjusted earnings per share in a range of $3.15 to $3.25, above Wall Street's expectations of earnings per share of $3.14. However, its anticipated revenue decline of 1% is weaker than expected; analysts were forecasting net sales growth of 1.4%.
Starbucks is projecting North American same-store sales growth of 4% for the fiscal year.
The company's earnings and revenue outlook includes an additional week and the effects of the shift in its China business to a joint venture business model. Starbucks is also projecting slight deflation in coffee prices and slowing net new North American cafe openings, which will both weigh on its full-year revenue, according to CFO Cathy Smith.
Shares of Starbucks fell nearly 2% in extended trading.
Here's what the company reported for the quarter ended Sept. 27 compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
Starbucks reported fiscal fourth-quarter net income attributable to the company of $677.2 million, or 59 cents per share, up from $133.1 million, or 12 cents per share, a year earlier.
Excluding restructuring and impairment costs and other items, the company reported earnings per share of 80 cents.
Net revenue fell 4% to $9.14 billion, reflecting the joint venture deal in China.
The company's global same-store sales increased 7.2%, fueled by growth in average ticket, and beating Wall Street estimates of 6%, according to StreetAccount. Transactions grew 1.8% in the quarter.
Starbucks' U.S. cafes reported same-store sales growth of 7.7%, topping StreetAccount estimates of a 6.5% increase.
Under Niccol's "Back to Starbucks" strategy, the company has focused on improving service, making its cafes more welcoming and sharpening its marketing. The changes have helped to win back customers.
"Starbucks brand affinity is at near record levels as our menu innovation, marketing and merchandise continue to create moments that drive culture and bring people into our coffee houses," Niccol told analysts.
The company said its North American rollout of its fall menu, which includes the iconic pumpkin spice latte, was the company's strongest ever autumn launch day. And matcha is now a $1 billion drink for Starbucks.
Outside of North America, the company's international comparable sales ticked up 0.9%, as traffic declines offset an increase to average ticket. That growth fell short of analyst estimates of a 3.2% increase, according to StreetAccount.
After its China business transitioned to a joint venture, Starbucks has shifted most of its international business to a licensed model, allowing local operators to take charge. The company is also exploring selling a majority stake in its Japan business, Reuters reported in September.
Starbucks opened 303 net new cafes during the quarter. In September, the company announced it would close about 1% of its North American footprint, or about 250 locations, as part of its turnaround.
By the end of its fiscal year, across the U.S. and Canada, the company also completed more than 1,700 cafe uplifts, meant to make its stores more welcoming to customers. The company has said locations that receive a makeover, with tweaks like increased seating and softer lighting, see higher transactions in the aftermath.
